units.text: Welcome. Over the next hour or so, we are going to tell the story of one of the strangest and most successful countries in Europe: the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
It is small. You could drive across it in about an hour.
Its population is smaller than that of many a single city.
And yet it has been fought over by emperors and kings for more than a thousand years.
It has been a fortress, a province, a battlefield, a steel empire, a banking center, and one of the founding members of the European Union.
It is the last grand duchy in the world.
How did a tiny territory on the edge of the great powers end up with all of that history?
The answer is a story of rock, iron, borders, and stubbornness.
It is a story of a people who, in the words of their own national motto, want to remain what they are.
We will move in order, from the Stone Age to the present day.
Settle in, and let's begin with a swap of land beside a river.
